newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac, Major agree joint efforts on Zaire aid.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, Major agree joint efforts on Zaire aid.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac and British Prime Minister John Major agreed on Friday to closely coordinate their efforts to help refugees in Zaire after Major signalled Britain might send troops.

"The two countries have agreed to coordinate their efforts closely, especially within the framework of the United Nations Security Council and the European Union" to help ensure aid reaches refugees, the two said in a joint statement at a Franco-British summit.

The statement did not mention sending troops but said the two wanted international arrangements "swiftly put in place to enable humanitarian aid reliably to reach displaced persons and refugees once again."
However, the French version of the joint statement said: "They declared themselves prepared to contribute." The phrase was not included in the English text.
The two leaders said the longer term objective was "enabling the voluntary return of these people to their country of origin." The two would also seek a longer-term political solution.
Major said in an interview with BBC radio that sending troops was a possibility but that it was too early to decide. About 1.2 million refugees are threatened by fighting in eastern Zaire.
